metadata.title: Total Generalized Variation
metadata.actual_title: Optimization of optode configurations for fluorescence optical tomography by experimental design methods
metadata.actual_authors: Manuel Freiberger, Christian Clason, Hermann Scharfetter
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Diffusion equation with fluorophore concentration
nodes.statement: With spatially variable fluorophore concentration $c$, $-\nabla\cdot(\kappa(x,\lambda)\nabla\varphi(x)) + (\mu_{a,i}(x,\lambda) + c(x)\varepsilon(\lambda) + i\omega/v)\varphi(x) = q(x)$ with boundary condition $\varphi(x) + 2R\kappa(x,\lambda)\partial_n\varphi(x) = 0$ and $\kappa = (3(\mu_{a,i} + c\varepsilon + \mu_s'))^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Diffusion approximation of light propagation in tissue including fluorophore absorption, with Robin boundary condition.

nodes.name: Coupled excitation/emission system
nodes.statement: Two coupled diffusion equations: $A_{ex}(c)\varphi_{ex} = q$ and $A_{em}(c)\varphi_{em} = B(c)\varphi_{ex}$, with $B(c)\varphi_{ex}(x) = (Q/(1-i\omega\tau))\,c(x)\varepsilon_{ex}\varphi_{ex}(x)$ where $Q$ is quantum yield and $\tau$ fluorescence lifetime.
nodes.statement_clean: Operator system coupling excitation and emission photon-density fields through the fluorophore.

nodes.name: Boundary measurement
nodes.statement: A measurement is $d := v\int_{\partial\Omega}(1/(2R))\delta(x - x_D)\varphi_{em}(x)\,dx$, the photon flux leaving at detector point $x_D$. The $i$-th source/detector pair gives $d_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: A measurement is the boundary photon flux at a detector location, expressed as a linear functional of the emission field.

nodes.name: Nonlinear forward operator
nodes.statement: Write the coupled PDE system as $F(c,\varphi(c)) = 0$ where $\varphi=(\varphi_{ex},\varphi_{em})$ and $F:(c,\varphi)\mapsto (A_{ex}(c)\varphi_{ex} - q,\ A_{em}(c)\varphi_{em} - B(c)\varphi_{ex})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combined nonlinear operator equation expressing the forward problem as F(c, phi) = 0.

nodes.name: Sensitivity (Jacobian) matrix
nodes.statement: Discretizing $c$ with piecewise-constant ansatz functions yields the Jacobian/sensitivity matrix $J$ where $J_{ij}$ is the effect of a concentration change in element $j$ on measurement $i$. Linearization: $\Delta d = J(c_0)\Delta c$.
nodes.statement_clean: Finite-element Jacobian linking concentration perturbations to measurement perturbations.

nodes.name: Source-partitioned sensitivity
nodes.statement: With $\mathcal{M}$ all measurements and $S_i\subset\mathcal{M}$ those using source $i$, partition $J=\begin{pmatrix}J_1\\J_2\end{pmatrix}$, $d=\begin{pmatrix}d_1\\d_2\end{pmatrix}$ where $J_2,d_2$ collect rows for source $i$ and $J_1,d_1$ the rest.
nodes.statement_clean: Row partition of the sensitivity matrix induced by selecting one source.

nodes.name: Entropy and mutual information of measurements
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathrm{cov}(c)=\sigma_c I$, so $\mathrm{cov}(d)=\sigma_c JJ^T$. Then $H(d)=\tfrac{1}{2}\log((2\pi e)^{|\mathcal{M}|}\det\mathrm{cov}(d))$, $H(d_1|d_2)=\tfrac{1}{2}\log((2\pi e)^{|\mathcal{M}|-|S_i|}\det\mathrm{cov}(d_1|d_2))$, and $\mathrm{MI}(d_1,d_2):=H(d_1)-H(d_1|d_2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gaussian entropy and conditional entropy of measurements, with mutual information defined as the entropy reduction.

nodes.name: Redundancy of a source (arithmetic)
nodes.statement: $r_i := \frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i|\,|S_i|}\sum_{m\in S_i}\sum_{n\in\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i}\frac{(j_m,j_n)^2}{\|j_m\|^2\|j_n\|^2} \in [0,1]$, the average squared cosine between rows of $J$ from source $i$ and other sources.
nodes.statement_clean: Average squared cosine between Jacobian rows of source i and all other measurements; high values mean source i is redundant.

nodes.name: Arithmetic quality measure
nodes.statement: $q_i := 1 - r_i = 1 - \frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i|\,|S_i|}\sum_{m\in S_i}\sum_{n\in\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i}\frac{(j_m,j_n)^2}{\|j_m\|^2\|j_n\|^2}$. Analogous expression holds for detectors using $D_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quality criterion (one minus redundancy) used to rank sources/detectors in the selection algorithm.

nodes.name: Geometric quality measure
nodes.statement: $q_{g,i} := \prod_{n\in\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i}\Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{|S_i|}\sum_{m\in S_i}\frac{(j_m,j_n)^2}{\|j_m\|^2\|j_n\|^2}\Bigr)^{1/|\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i|}$, replacing one sum by a product to obtain a closer link to entropy optimization.
nodes.statement_clean: Geometric-mean variant of the redundancy quality criterion that aligns more closely with mutual-information minimization.

nodes.name: Focused sensitivity matrix
nodes.statement: Given a weighting mask $f$ with $0\le f_i\le 1$ on the region of interest (binary or smooth), define $J_F := J\,\mathrm{diag}(f)$, used in place of $J$ to bias the optimization toward a region.
nodes.statement_clean: Column-weighted sensitivity matrix used to focus the optimal design on a given region of interest.

nodes.name: Frechet differentiability of forward map
nodes.statement: Since $F$ is continuous and Frechet-differentiable in $c$ and $\varphi$, the implicit function theorem gives $\varphi(c)$ Frechet-differentiable in $c$ with $\partial_\varphi F(c,\varphi(c))\,\varphi'(c) = -\partial_c F(c,\varphi(c))$, provided $\partial_\varphi F(c,\varphi(c))$ is bijective.
nodes.statement_clean: The forward map c -> phi(c) is Frechet-differentiable, by the Banach-space implicit function theorem.
assumptions: $F$ is continuous and Frechet-differentiable in $c$ and $\varphi$

nodes.name: Bijectivity of partial derivative
nodes.statement: Since $F$ is linear in $\varphi$, $\partial_\varphi F(c,\varphi(c))\,\delta\varphi = (A_{ex}(c)\delta\varphi_{ex},\ A_{em}(c)\delta\varphi_{em} - B(c)\delta\varphi_{ex})$, and bijectivity follows from well-posedness of the forward problem.
nodes.statement_clean: Partial derivative of F with respect to phi is bijective, by well-posedness of the forward PDE system.

nodes.name: Conditional covariance via Schur complement
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{cov}(d_1|d_2) = \sigma_c\bigl(J_1 J_1^T - J_1 J_2^T (J_2 J_2^T)^{-1} J_2 J_1^T\bigr)$, valid because $J_2 J_2^T$ is invertible (the rows of $J$ are linearly independent and $J$ has many more columns than rows).
nodes.statement_clean: Closed form for the conditional covariance of d_1 given d_2 using the Schur complement of J_2 J_2^T.
nodes.origin_citation: Puntanen & Styan, The Schur Complement and Its Applications (2005)

nodes.name: Mutual information in matrix form
nodes.statement: $-\mathrm{MI}(d_1,d_2) = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\bigl(I - (J_1 J_1^T)^{-1/2} J_1 J_2^T (J_2 J_2^T)^{-1} J_2 J_1^T (J_1 J_1^T)^{-1/2}\bigr)$, assuming $J_1 J_1^T$ has an invertible square root.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form matrix expression for the negative mutual information between two measurement subsets.
assumptions: $J_1 J_1^T$ admits an invertible square root

nodes.name: Matrix form of arithmetic quality measure
nodes.statement: $q_i = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i|}\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(I - \tfrac{1}{|S_i|}\mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T)\,J_1 J_2^T\,\mathrm{diag}^{-1}(J_2 J_2^T)\,J_2 J_1^T\,\mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T)\bigr)$, derived from the Frobenius-norm interpretation of $r_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Trace-based matrix expression for the arithmetic quality measure q_i.
assumptions: diagonal of $J_1 J_1^T$ has positive entries
conclusions: $q_i$ admits the trace-based closed form above

nodes.name: Matrix form of geometric quality measure
nodes.statement: $q_{g,i} = \det\bigl(\mathrm{diag}(I - \tfrac{1}{|S_i|}\mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T) J_1 J_2^T \mathrm{diag}^{-1}(J_2 J_2^T) J_2 J_1^T \mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T))\bigr)^{1/|\mathcal{M}\setminus S_i|}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Determinant-based matrix form of the geometric quality measure, paralleling the trace form for q_i.
assumptions: diagonal of $J_1 J_1^T$ has positive entries
conclusions: $q_{g,i}$ admits the determinant-based closed form above

nodes.name: Redundancy decrease tends to decrease MI (heuristic)
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz, $\mathrm{cov}^2(x,y) \le \mathrm{var}(x)\mathrm{var}(y)$, so reducing variances also reduces covariances; hence a decrease in $q_{g,i}$ tends to decrease $-\mathrm{MI}$ and thus increase mutual information of source $i$ with the rest.
nodes.statement_clean: Heuristic argument that decreasing the geometric redundancy implies decreasing mutual information.
conclusions: A decrease in $q_{g,i}$ implies a decrease in $-\mathrm{MI}$ (heuristic)

nodes.name: Sensitivity computation via implicit function formulation
nodes.statement: Compute the Jacobian $J$ of $d$ with respect to $c$ by solving the coupled forward system, then two perturbation BVPs per optode using the implicit function representation.

nodes.name: Redundancy-minimization optode selection
nodes.statement: Greedy top-down algorithm that iteratively removes the source/detector with the lowest quality measure $q_i$ (or $q_{g,i}$) until a stopping criterion is met.
input: Initial pool of feasible source and detector optodes
Stopping criterion (e.g., target number of sources and detectors)
output: Optimized subset of source and detector optodes minimizing redundancy

nodes.name: Optode selection problem
nodes.section: 1 Introduction / 3 Optimization of the measurement setup
nodes.statement: Given an initial pool of source and detector optodes and a target number to retain, choose the subset whose Jacobian rows are as mutually independent as possible (i.e., minimum total redundancy / maximum mutual information).
nodes.statement_clean: Pick a subset of optodes that maximizes information, equivalently minimizes redundancy among Jacobian rows.

nodes.name: Pseudo-inverse interpretation of Schur complement term
nodes.statement: The factor $J_2^\dagger := J_2^T(J_2 J_2^T)^{-1}$ in Eq. (21) is the pseudo-inverse of $J_2$. If $J_2^\dagger J_2 = I$ exactly, $\mathrm{cov}(d_1)$ vanishes: $d_2$ already determines all model parameters.

nodes.name: Computational infeasibility of MI criterion
nodes.statement: Direct minimization of $-\mathrm{MI}(d_1,d_2)$ via Eq. (24) requires repeated matrix inversions, square roots, and determinants, making it computationally infeasible at the scale of interest. The redundancy-reduction algorithm is used as a tractable surrogate.

nodes.name: NP-hardness of full search and greedy limitation
nodes.statement: An exhaustive search over all subsets is NP-hard ($\sim 10^{18}$ configurations for the example geometry). The greedy top-down algorithm cannot guarantee a global minimum; stochastic methods are mentioned as a possible alternative.

nodes.name: Cylinder phantom with three focus regions
nodes.statement: Optimize 8 sources and 8 detectors from an initial pool of 48+48 in a zig-zag pattern on six rings (cylinder height 90 mm, radius 30 mm), focusing on three regions A, B, C; FE mesh has approx. 30,000 elements.
nodes.statement_clean: Numerical example applying the algorithm on a cylindrical phantom with three different focus regions A, B, C.

nodes.name: Reconstruction with three spherical perturbations
nodes.statement: Reconstructions from synthetic measurements generated by a finer FE mesh containing three 5-mm spherical fluorophore perturbations, using the optimized geometric-averaging optode setups for regions A, B, C.
nodes.statement_clean: Reconstruction example illustrating how focused designs suppress fluorophore signal outside the focus region.

nodes.name: Singular-value comparison of full vs focused designs
nodes.statement: Singular-value analysis (Table 2): full pool of optodes has condition number $\sim 6\cdot 10^{12}$, while focused designs reduce the condition number by at least $10^6$; arithmetic averaging gives condition numbers about 4x smaller than geometric averaging.
nodes.statement_clean: Quantitative comparison of condition numbers for full vs optimized configurations and for arithmetic vs geometric averaging.

nodes.name: Proof: matrix form of the arithmetic quality measure
nodes.statement: Rewrite $r_i$ as the squared Frobenius norm of $\mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T) J_1 J_2^T \mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_2 J_2^T)$, then use $\|A\|_F^2 = \mathrm{tr}(AA^T)$ and substitute $q_i = 1 - r_i$.

nodes.name: Frobenius-norm rewrite of $r_i$
nodes.statement: Express the double sum in $r_i$ (Eq. 26) as the sum of squared entries of $\mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_1 J_1^T) J_1 J_2^T \mathrm{diag}^{-1/2}(J_2 J_2^T)$, identifying it with the squared Frobenius norm.

nodes.name: Trace identity
nodes.statement: Use $\|A\|_F^2 = \mathrm{tr}(A A^T)$ to convert the Frobenius-norm expression into a trace, yielding the matrix form of $r_i$ (Eq. 31).

nodes.name: Substitute $q_i = 1 - r_i$
nodes.statement: Combine with $q_i = 1 - r_i$ and pull the identity inside the trace to obtain Eq. (32).

nodes.name: Initialize feasible pool
nodes.statement: Set the current pool of sources and detectors to the initial feasible set; specify a stopping criterion (e.g., target number of sources/detectors).

nodes.name: Assemble (focused) sensitivity
nodes.statement: Compute the Jacobian $J$ for the current pool; if focusing is desired, replace $J$ by $J_F = J\,\mathrm{diag}(f)$.

nodes.name: Score and remove worst source
nodes.statement: For each source $i$ in the pool, compute $q_i$ (Eq. 32) or $q_{g,i}$ (Eq. 33); remove the source achieving the lowest quality.

nodes.name: Score and remove worst detector
nodes.statement: Repeat the scoring with $S_i$ replaced by detector index set $D_i$; remove the detector with the lowest quality.

nodes.name: Check stopping criterion and return
nodes.statement: If the stopping criterion is met (e.g., desired number of sources and detectors reached), return the current pool; otherwise loop back to step 2.
